notes: SCOPE (second round, 16 Oct 2026): covered are the 14 acs5_* (fairfield-county included), 14 acs1_*, 3 bea_*, 7 pep_* (Vintage 2023, Census Data API) and 3 cbp_* (CBP 2023, Census Data API, NAICS 2017) series. NOT covered: the permit series (removed from the register). Nothing under _cache/markets/held/ and none of the pipeline scripts were opened. The PEP check of round one (Vintage 2025 files) is replaced by the Vintage 2023 API pull.

Method: every expected cell is derived from the raw files by code in this script (ACS Data API JSON by level, geoinfo CBSA member lists, BEA CAINC1 full rows keyed by file level, PEP V2023 July 1 rows, CBP all-industry rows with the 2- to 6-digit parent codes, the 2020 Census Connecticut county subdivisions) and the market rules of D39/D40; compositions come from geographies.json markets[].composition_source and resolved{counties, places, cousubs, cbsa, ct_planning_regions, ct_legacy_counties}; CBP classes from naics-map.json legacy['2017'] (no class fall back to naics2022). Tolerances: counts exact, dollars within 0.5, shares within 1e-6, CBP per-10,000 within 0.006 (lower bound) with up_to exact, MOE within 0.0101 (the register rounds to 2 decimals).

CBP SECTOR-RANGE FINDING. The API publishes the 2-digit level of NAICS 31-33, 44-45 and 48-49 only as the ranges '31-33', '44-45', '48-49'. Primary reading (used for the headline numbers): that range IS the 2-digit parent of its codes, so a class code absent at a geography whose nearest published parent is the sector range gets that sector's gap (sector establishments less its published 6-digit children) in up_to. The register looks for the two-digit string itself ('44', '48'...), which is never published, so it skips the sector range: a class in those sectors with no 3-, 4- or 5-digit parent published at a geography is left out as zero with nothing withheld (or carries a smaller up_to), although up to the sector gap may be hidden. Effect on the census: 43206 class cells differ from the primary reading (cbp_estab 14402, cbp_emp 14402, cbp_estab_per_10k 14402), every one explained by this single rule (re-deriving with the literal two-digit lookup reproduces the register cell exactly); 30 further problems are not explained by it (the Puerto Rico CBSA entries of the next note). Geographies affected by the sector rule: {'cbp_emp': 3315, 'cbp_estab': 3315, 'cbp_estab_per_10k': 3315}. 2 of the 797 sampled values differ from the primary reading because of this rule. Lower-bound values (the sum of published 6-digit cells) agree in every case; only up_to and the presence of an otherwise-absent class differ. County sets agree with the sum of their counties' cells (value and up_to) under either reading.
